summary: Made Modbus TCP symmetric with MQTT for actuation, and gave the profile/device editor a Modbus-aware authoring UI. `entities.ProfileCommand` gained `Transport` (""/"mqtt" default, or "modbus"), `Register`, `RegKind` (u16/i16), and `ScaleFactor`. `CommandService.Issue` now branches to a new `sendModbus` when a command's transport is Modbus, AFTER every existing gate (read-only-by-default, admin-only, declared bounds, rate limit, audit, never-auto-retried) -- Modbus actuation inherits the identical safety gates MQTT commands have always gone through, it is not a parallel, looser path. `sendModbus` encodes the value via a new `encodeRegister` helper (applies the read-side scale in reverse: raw = round(value / scaleFactor); range-checks against the declared RegKind; only single-register u16/i16 are written, u32/i32 are refused rather than half-written) and performs the write through a `modbusWrite` seam (production = `infra/iot/modbus.WriteConfirm`, a guarded write-then-read-back that never re-issues, bounded by a new 5s `modbusWriteTimeout`; a fake in tests). A successful guarded write sets the command straight to `confirmed` (stronger than MQTT's `sent`, since the device already reported the value back) rather than waiting on a separately-reported telemetry reading; a lost/unconfirmed write ends the command `failed`, audited, exactly like an MQTT refusal, and is never retried. `services.SaveProfileCommand` and `ProfileService.replaceCommands` carry the four new fields through the profile CRUD path unchanged in shape from the pre-existing MQTT fields. Separately, the backend already supported custom Modbus device profiles (Transport/ModbusMode/ModbusBase/PollSeconds, per-key Register/RegKind/ScaleFactor/WordSwap, device Endpoint/Unit) from the prior SunSpec driver-foundation work, but the frontend profile editor was MQTT-shaped only; it is now transport-aware: a Transport toggle (MQTT / Modbus TCP) on the profile editor reveals Modbus mode (SunSpec auto-discover vs. an explicit register map), base register and poll-seconds fields; each telemetry key's JSON-path input becomes a register/regKind/scaleFactor/word-swap binding for a register-map profile; and each command's MQTT topic/payload/confirm-key inputs become a register/regKind/scaleFactor write binding (no confirm-key needed -- the write confirms itself by read-back). The device create/edit forms now show an Endpoint (host:port) + Unit id field in place of the broker password when the chosen profile is Modbus. New i18n keys added across en/ms/zh/ar for all of the above.
compatibility: Fully additive and backward-compatible for every existing install. No shipped built-in profile declares a Modbus command yet (both generic-sunspec-solar and huawei-sun2000 remain read-only), so no existing device's behavior changes: a command's default Transport is empty, which still means "mqtt", and every pre-existing MQTT command continues to publish exactly as before -- the new branch in Issue is only taken when a command's declaration explicitly sets Transport="modbus". Existing Modbus device profiles (read-only, from the earlier SunSpec work) are unaffected; the new UI fields only appear when a profile's Transport is Modbus and are additive to the existing create/edit forms. Authoring a Modbus command requires a correctly-configured Register/RegKind/ScaleFactor per the target device's Modbus map -- getting this wrong writes a wrong value to real hardware, so it should be tuned against documentation or a simulator (tools/sunspec-sim, which honours writes) before pointing at production equipment. The myiotsan_commands_total metric counts Modbus confirmed/failed outcomes at parity with the MQTT path.
